payload.feature:
This worktree carries the verifier and shipper as boxed exec gates as delivered by five runs on top of main aa9394c (two more were lit and superseded before their first seat finished, as a later CI report arrived), the last being this-worktree-carries-the-verifi-64d39271 at commit 078730f, shipped clean. Its pull request, #173, still fails the macOS and Windows test jobs on two distinct defects, and this slice answers both on top of the existing commits and ships. Keep every property the seven commits established.

The failure. Thirteen brokkr-store unit tests fail on macOS at crates/brokkr-store/src/tests.rs:8:5 — the `store()` helper asserts `store.path() == path` and gets

  left:  "/private/var/folders/d8/…/T/.tmpgsC2i1/forge.db"
  right: "/var/folders/d8/…/T/.tmpgsC2i1/forge.db"

because this branch's crates/brokkr-store/src/lib.rs now canonicalizes the path in `Store::open` (added so the ship seat receives the engine's actual journal path) while the helper compares against the un-canonicalized temp path; on Linux /tmp is not a symlink, so every run here passed. These failures were masked on the earlier heads because `cargo test` stops at the first failing test binary and the brokkr-cli binary failed first.

Fix it at the right layer, and say which in the commit: either `Store::open` keeps reporting the path it was given — canonicalization belongs to the caller that needed a stable path (the ship seat's journal argument, the ledger verb), and the one store test that was adjusted to expect a canonical path (`reader.path() == db.canonicalize()`) is restored — or, if the store's canonical path is load-bearing for a behaviour a test pins, the `store()` helper and every store test compare canonical paths and the doc comment on `Store::path` says the path is canonical. Prefer the first: a store that reports a different path than it was opened with is a surprise to every caller, and the ship seat's need is local.

Then sweep, because this is the third platform-only defect of the same shape: grep the whole workspace for tests that compare a path derived from `tempfile::tempdir()` (or `TempDir`) against a path the product reports or prints — `assert_eq!` on paths, `contains` on displayed paths, `ends_with`, `starts_with` — and make each one honest where the temp directory is a symlink (macOS) or canonical paths carry a verbatim prefix (Windows): canonicalize both sides, or compare as `Path`s component by component, never as strings with a separator inside a component. State the rule once in a comment at the store helper and refer to it elsewhere.

The second failure, Windows only. `engine::tests::an_exec_seat_with_hands_is_boxed_whole` in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/tests.rs:3833 fails with

  left:  "/runtime/bundle\\scripts/verify.sh"
  right: "/runtime/bundle/scripts/verify.sh"

The path of a script inside the box is built by joining the bound bundle root `/runtime/bundle` with the `./`-relative entry using the host's `Path::join`, so on Windows the separator is a backslash. A box is a Linux namespace: every path inside it is a POSIX path whatever the host that composed it. Build in-box paths as strings joined with `/` (a small helper beside the box argv builder, documented as "paths inside the namespace are POSIX paths, never host paths"), use it for the bundle root bind, the worktree mount and every `./` expansion that lands inside the box, and let the test run on every platform rather than gating it — the composition is pure string work and should be right everywhere. Sweep the hands module and the engine's `hands_command` for any other `PathBuf::join` whose result is a path inside the namespace.

And give CI the tool that would have shown all of this at once: in .github/workflows/ci.yml the test job's `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` gains `--no-fail-fast`, so a platform job reports every failing binary in one run rather than one per push; the MSRV job's test line likewise if it runs tests.

Constraints: the exact coverage gate (scripts/coverage-exact.sh, run with stdin closed: </dev/null) must stay at literal 100%; clippy -D warnings and fmt must stay clean; cargo test --workspace green here and, by construction, on macOS and Windows; contracts/, fixtures/ and policy/phase-machine.json are read-only; the decision index docs/decisions/README.md must keep every row main carries in number order; do not name the private neighbours in prose; commit in the repository's style on top of 078730f and never push.

result.notes: Kept Store::path faithful to the caller, canonicalized the journal only at the ship/ledger boundary, rendered all in-box paths as POSIX paths, made temp-path assertions component-aware across platforms, and enabled CI --no-fail-fast. Workspace tests, fmt, clippy -D warnings, and literal 100% exact coverage pass; committed as 1a4c1b7.

cargo test --workspace: 57 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed 1a4c1b7 (the one commit on top of 078730f) for correctness, simplicity and security. Verified here: cargo fmt --check clean; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast green; exact coverage re-derived with cargo +nightly llvm-cov --branch --lcov and the gate's own DA/BRDA/FN-by-start-line rules: 17490/17490 lines, 2660/2660 branches, 1661/1661 functions, no harness file in the report (scripts/coverage-exact.sh itself is blocked for this seat, so the same commands were run by hand). contracts/, fixtures/, policy/phase-machine.json and docs/decisions/README.md untouched; tree clean. Correctness: the store reports the path it was opened with again (framing's preferred layer, said in the subject), the read-only test is restored, both ship-seat sites canonicalize locally; namespace_join builds in-box paths with '/' so the Windows test passes by construction, the test stays ungated, the argv test that names host paths is already #[cfg(unix)]; the box binds and env values went through namespace_path (identity on Linux); ci.yml test job has --no-fail-fast and the MSRV job only runs cargo check so was rightly left alone; the sweep converted every tempdir-vs-reported string comparison I could find to Path comparisons. Security: none. namespace_join only receives a strip_prefix remainder so the traversal surface is what Path::join gave before; bwrap-absent refusal, clearenv, mask binds and read-only bundle mount unchanged; --no-fail-fast does not alter CI exit status. Residual findings, none above low: (1) LOW correctness, pre-existing across the seven commits, not introduced here: Engine::runtime_hands compares a canonical journal against a canonical workdir, but hands_command binds the workdir at self.workdir() as given; with a --repo spelled through a symlink and a worktree-local journal, context.journal (canonical) has no bind inside the box and the ship seat cannot open it (fails closed, so not security). (2) INFO simplicity: the journal canonicalize expression is duplicated at engine.rs:786 and :917; a one-line journal_path() helper would state the rule once. (3) INFO simplicity: namespace_path(Path::new(SANDBOX_BUNDLE)) wraps a POSIX literal; s(SANDBOX_BUNDLE) read plainer. (4) INFO test-strength: driver_conformance now checks that the locator's last component starts with seat- rather than its third component, marginally weaker than the old prefix. (5) INFO: the temp-path rule is stated at the store helper and referred to from the engine test only; the cli/protocol sites changed by the sweep carry no back-reference.
